title: Data-based Numerical Simulation of Buoyant Jet Flow
subtitle: Master's Thesis · Step 1 — CFD reference, rCFD workflow & face-swap-diffusion sweep
author: Mochamad Bukhori Zainun (k12438440)
institution: Department of Particulate Flow Modelling, JKU Linz
abstract: A short CFD run records the recurring flow patterns of a laminar buoyant jet in a closed water tank. Recurrence-CFD (rCFD) then replays those patterns to transport the temperature field at a fraction of the cost, with a face-swap diffusion operator (parameter f_sd) restoring the missing mixing.

groups.heading: Key findings
items: rCFD reproduces the 600 s buoyant-jet temperature transport from one short CFD run.
Best mixing strength is metric-dependent: f_sd = 0.000 for mean temperature, f_sd = 0.500 for thermal centre of gravity (CoG RMSE 0.069 mm).
The CoG optimum is broad (0.375–0.750), not knife-edge.

groups.heading: Physical interpretation
items: A warm laminar jet (Re ≈ 100) rises by buoyancy and builds a stable warm layer under the ceiling.
Two counter-rotating vortices form from entrainment; buoyancy tilts them upward.
Mixing beyond what the shift map carries is supplied by the face-swap operator.

groups.heading: Numerical stability
items: Structured 1 mm cubic cells (~85,625) keep the C2C shift maps exact.
Face-swap diffusion is mass- and energy-conservative; above the 1/8 cap it splits into inner sweeps.
Laminar solver matches the regime, avoiding spurious turbulent mixing.

groups.heading: AI / data-driven contribution
items: rCFD is data-based: recurring flow patterns are learned once and replayed, the same spirit as ML surrogates.
Average speed-up ~263× (120–701× across the sweep), compute-only.
The single knob f_sd is the tunable parameter a future learned model could optimise.

references.text: Lichtenegger, T. & Pirker, S. (2016). Recurrence CFD — a novel approach to simulate multiphase flows with strongly separated time scales. Chemical Engineering Science, 153, 394–410.
Pirker, S. & Lichtenegger, T. (2018). Efficient time-extrapolation of single- and multiphase simulations by transport-based recurrence CFD. Chemical Engineering Science, 188, 65–83.
